Lambda reported healthy on just 36.1 percent of observations since August 14, 2026, making it a pronounced outlier in a dataset where every other provider reached at least 91 percent.

Most of the twelve providers cluster tightly near perfect availability. Five, AssemblyAI, Cohere, Deepgram, Groq, and Stability AI, recorded 100 percent across roughly 103 observations each. Six more fell between 97 and 99 percent. That narrow band suggests the technical floor for running a public inference API is already high across much of the market, at least over this roughly three-week window.

OpenAI is the second-lowest at 91.3 percent, which is notable given its position in the market, but the data does not explain causes. Lambda's 36.1 percent stands in a different category entirely, more than 55 points below OpenAI, and its slightly lower observation count of 97 hints at possible measurement gaps alongside genuine outages. Neither figure can be attributed here to power, infrastructure, or compute-layer failures specifically; the data records outcomes, not causes.

The daily series shows eleven providers healthy on most days, dropping to ten on four occasions. The window covers nineteen days, which is long enough to distinguish persistent problems from brief incidents but short enough that a single prolonged outage can dominate a provider's aggregate. What the data does not cover is historical trends before August 14, incident duration, or any weighting by traffic volume, so a provider with a short but total blackout and one with intermittent degradation can produce similar percentages.
